methodology: Contests and candidate names are from the SF Department of Elections candidate list for Nov 3, 2026 (sf.gov), Ballotpedia (local) and Wikipedia's 2026 California elections page (statewide). Local measure letters and official titles are from the Department of Elections qualified measures page. Vote counts: KQED's San Francisco results page (AP and county data; latest stamp 11:53 p.m. PT Nov 3) for U.S. House and Assembly, and the SF Standard results page (updated 7 a.m. PT Nov 4) for supervisors, school boards, measures and statewide totals; the two agree on every measure count. Supervisor figures are the final ranked-choice round shown by the SF Standard, with first-choice votes alongside; KQED's first-choice figures differ slightly. Calls come from KQED's called-race stamps, the SF Standard, Mission Local, the Bay Area Reporter and SF Chronicle headlines, as cited on each race. The sfelections.org results pages, sos.ca.gov, the Department of Elections voter pamphlet PDF and several news results pages could not be opened (permission not granted in this session). Parties for statewide candidates are from Wikipedia; for House and Assembly from KQED and Ballotpedia. Positions were not gathered for this file. The 'what' text is a general description of each office. The Superior Court Seat 16 contest is not listed because no source opened confirmed it was on the November ballot.
